chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Ibn Miskān, from Abān ibn Taghlib, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about one who is killed in the way of Allah: is he given ghusl, shrouded, and embalmed with ḥanūṭ?

He said: "He is buried as he is, in his clothes, unless there remains some life in him and then he dies; in that case he is given ghusl, shrouded, embalmed with ḥanūṭ, and salat is performed over him.
Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed salat over Ḥamzah and shrouded him because he had been stripped."

key_terms.جُرِّدَ: he was stripped of his clothing
key_terms.رَمَقٌ: a remaining trace of life or last vitality
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: in the way of Allah; referring here to being killed as a martyr
key_terms.يُحَنَّطُ: he is embalmed with ḥanūṭ, the prescribed funerary perfume
key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: funeral salat is performed over him
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: he is given ghusl, the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.يُكَفَّنُ: he is shrouded in burial cloth

ai.seo_question: Does a martyr killed in the way of Allah receive ghusl and kafan before burial?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the one killed in the way of Allah. A martyr who dies immediately is buried in his clothes without ghusl, but if some life remains and he dies afterward, the normal funerary rites are performed. The report also cites the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding Ḥamzah as supporting precedent.
